Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write a short announcement for a new feature in a note-taking app: offline sync. Around 200 words.

Offline sync is now live in version 3.2.

Until now, editing a note without a connection meant your changes sat on that device until you reopened the app somewhere with signal. Now the app keeps a full local copy of your notebook and reconciles it the moment a connection returns. Write on a plane, on a subway, in a basement office with one bar. The changes queue up and land where they belong.

Conflicts get handled per paragraph rather than per note. If you edit the third paragraph on your laptop and someone on your shared notebook edits the first, both edits survive. When two people touch the same paragraph, you'll see both versions side by side with timestamps and can pick one or merge by hand. No more "Copy 2" files cluttering your folders.

Sync status shows in the bottom left: a filled dot when everything has landed, a hollow one with a count when changes are still queued. Tap it to see exactly which notes are waiting.

The local copy is encrypted with the same key as your synced data, so an offline device holds nothing readable without your passcode.

Available today on iOS, Android, and desktop. Web offline support is in beta behind a settings toggle, and we expect to ship it to everyone next month.

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Add a paragraph about what happens when two devices edit the same note offline.

Two devices offline at once is the case we spent the most time on. Say you draft on your laptop on a flight and your tablet, also offline, has an older copy you edit at the gate. Both queue their changes independently. When each one reconnects, the app replays the edits in the order they were made locally and merges them paragraph by paragraph, so the later reconnection does not overwrite the earlier one. Paragraphs neither device touched stay untouched. Where the two edits overlap, you get the same side-by-side view with a device name and timestamp on each version, and the note stays flagged in your sidebar until you resolve it.
